newsitem.title: UK: Crude tankers fixed to S.Korea, other sectors quiet.
newsitem.headline: Crude tankers fixed to S.Korea, other sectors quiet.

text.p: Plentiful crude tanker fixtures were seen on Monday to South Korea, home to one of the world's fastest growing refining industries.
From the Mideast Gulf, the 1993-built Tarim carrying 270,000 tonnes was fixed for Jan 14 at W62 for Ssangyong, which one broker said was representative for such a modern vessel
Another fairly new ship, the 1989-built World Pendant, was also fixed at W62 from the Gulf to South Korea with 252,500 tonnes, loading Jan 20, also for Ssangyong.

The Mediterranean was quiet, with many Italian brokers going home early due to heavy snow. "Not many fixtures are being reported but something is being done because some vessels are disappearing," an Italian broker said.

In U.K./Cont, an unusual fixture was the Olympic Faith with 130,000 tonnes Norway-Med, RNR for Statoil, loading Jan 10. The Sea Princess with 135,000 tonnes on a voyage Norway/USG at W75 for Statoil, loading Jan 6, also attracted some interest.
In West Africa the Stena Congress carrying 265,000 tonnes to the U.S. Gulf was fixed at W62.5 for BP, little changed from last week.
Nothing was fixed on fuel oil, a London broker said. He said notionally rates were W180 for 25,000 tonnes cross-UKC, "but some ships might do less to get fixed over the New Year."
A New York broker put 70,000 tonnes Caribs/upcoast at W160, about level with last week.
